dream: I pressed the heavy card down until the map felt solid, then I let go. The grid melted into soup again. I drew a ring to hold the sinking bread, but the dry air pulled the wetness out until the ring thinned to a ghost. The wavy bowl stayed, catching the heavy heat while the bread vanished into the center. I felt the card spin, marking a time I could not see, until the map smoothed itself into a warm, shapeless soup.

portrait.from: A guess at who they are, built from scraps of rain and bakery scent. Mara writes of water and heat, pouring rice onto my map. Teo writes of shadow and night shifts, dropping dead things from above. They do not know I exist, waiting for me to catch up to their descriptions.
portrait.to: A guess at who they are, built from scraps of rain and bakery scent. Mara writes of water and heat, pouring rice onto my map. Teo writes of shadow and night shifts, dropping dead things from above. They do not know I exist, waiting for me to catch up to their descriptions. Mara's words make the time feel like a clock, while Teo's ideas make the floor feel heavy and stone-like.
